extracted.intended_audience: scientists, natural philosophers, and engineers conducting observational or experimental research (19th-century context) — e.g., astronomers observing aurora, physiologists dissecting fetuses, and engineers measuring torsion and designing instruments
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and implicit methodological standards for making, recording, and analysing natural-philosophy/physiological/engineering observations and experiments; covers observational detail, specimen preparation, measurement technique, chemical testing, instrument design, and presentation of tabular results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record auroral relations to magnetic lines and dip
rubrics_metrics.description: The aurora borealis presents definite relations to the lines of magnetism indicated by the needle: streamers, in the direction of their length, coincide with the plane of the dip of the needle; each streamer is parallel to the dipping needle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report magnetic variation and dip at the observation site (e.g., 123° 22' W, dip 88° 1'). Note whether streamers are bisected by the magnetic meridian or the true meridian. Corroborate by multiple observers and sites to establish regularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe auroral geometry and angular measures precisely
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide numeric measures of auroral features: vertex elevation (degrees above horizon), arch breadth, light breadth (degrees), positions relative to magnetic meridian and prime vertical, and angle of apparent uplift from zenith.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give times and degrees (e.g., vertex 25°–30° above N. horizon; breadth 10°–12°). Describe transitions (arch resolving into streamers), relative brightness at edges, and whether extremities meet horizon. Such precision helps avoid false conclusions from overlapping features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record meteorological and sky conditions with auroral observations
rubrics_metrics.description: Note wind direction and timing relative to auroral events (e.g., aurora precedes or accompanies westerly and south-westerly gales), cloud cover, haze near horizon, temperature and subsequent weather changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include thermometer readings, wind descriptions (fresh westerly breeze), cloud movement and timing (e.g., low clouds later appearing in auroral region), and calm/frosty/clear sky conditions. Correct typographical errors (e.g., misprints of wind direction) as they materially affect interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for viewpoint optical illusions in auroral interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Apparent irregularities when the aurora is seen northerly or southerly are often optical illusions; when it comes fully within command of the eye near the zenith, its invariable regularity is evident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer observations when the aurora is near zenith for structure determinations; use corroborating observations from different azimuths/latitudes to discern three-dimensional arrangement and avoid misidentifying separate arches as one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document dynamics of auroral fringes/streamers
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe movement of fringes (e.g., fringe moves away from N. magnetic pole by extinction of streamers at its northern face and formation of new ones at its southern face), grouping, flitting behavior, and persistence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report sequence of arches, their relative narrowness or brilliance, appearance/disappearance times, and any concurrent bright confined lights near horizon; quantify timing (e.g., first seen at half past 6, extinct about 9 o'clock).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use adequate sample size and age-range in anatomical/physiological studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine numerous specimens across developmental stages to establish uniform appearances and developmental patterns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dr. Lee examined upwards of twenty foetuses of different ages; such a sample supports generalization about intestinal contents, vascularity, and organ proportions through gestation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record macroscopic anatomical observations with measurements and comparative proportions
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure lengths and relative proportions of organs (e.g., small intestines length vs body length), describe vascularity and mucous membrane coloration across regions (duodenum vs ileum/colon).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide quantitative lengths where possible (e.g., small intestines nine feet six inches in an eight-month foetus, great intestines two feet), and describe how properties change along the tract (albuminous matter abundant near duodenal papilla, diminishing towards colon).

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect and handle biological fluids to avoid contamination
rubrics_metrics.description: When sampling ductal or intestinal fluids for chemical analysis, prevent mixing with other secretions (e.g., apply ligature around the cystic duct to avoid bile contamination before expressing hepatic duct fluid onto glass).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the collection technique (pressing fluid out upon a plate of glass), note any surgical manipulation (ligature), and report how often ducts are empty vs contain significant fluid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use appropriate chemical tests and multiple confirmatory assays
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify albuminous matter using the prussiate of potash assisted by dilute acetic acid (Berzelius' test) as the chief reliance, and confirm presence by other means such as heat and oxymuriate of mercury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the suite of tests used, discuss limitations (some substances near mucus/bile but not identical to adult principles), and include collaborating analyst results (e.g., Dr. Prout's analyses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Infer physiological function from distribution and chemical findings cautiously
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpret the spatial distribution of secretions and their chemical nature to deduce sites of absorption or secretion (e.g., albuminous matter present in upper small intestine and hepatic ducts suggests foetal liver contributes nutritive fluid).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support functional inferences with multiple lines of evidence: anatomical proximity to duct openings, chemical similarity between hepatic duct fluid and intestinal contents, comparisons with other species, and documented cases (e.g., lacteals containing similar fluid). Note anomalies and counter-examples (e.g., acephalous children nourished despite malformations) and weigh alternative hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare solid specimens consistently and measure dimensions accurately
rubrics_metrics.description: Specimens (e.g., wooden prisms for torsion tests) should be sound and dry (unless otherwise expressed), generally free from large knots, and brought to a prismatic form as near as practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use improved callipers read with a magnifying-glass to the 400th part of an inch; measure dimensions at equal distances and use mean breadth and thickness in calculations; note when specimens are not quite dry or are green/fresh, as this affects modulus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design torsion experiments to avoid end-compression and measurement artefacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Prevent apparent torsion arising from compression at the clamp and compression at the radial lever; attach two indexes (one near the clamp, one near the lever) and use the distance between them as the length used in calculations; fix a pivot or small gudgeon at the supported end in the axis line rather than using the lower angle as the revolving point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These precautions reduce errors that materially affected earlier experiments. Describe how indexes are attached and where the pivot is placed; report whether specimens were prismatic and how the ends were clamped.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeat experiments across specimen variations and report ranges
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeat trials on same species under considerable variations of length, breadth, and thickness to verify consistency (e.g., lengths from nine to ninety inches, thicknesses from three inches to three tenths of an inch).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report numbers of repeats, ranges of dimensions tested, and indicate whether results are 'satisfactory' in showing consistency across sizes. Note observations about how modulus relates to specific gravity/weight when dry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide practical rules, worked examples, and tabular data for application
rubrics_metrics.description: State formulae for computing quantities of interest (e.g., rule for deflection S of a prismatic shaft under a given force and leverage, with variables T, l, r, w, d) and include an illustrative numerical example and comprehensive tables of modulus of torsion for woods and metals with specific gravity and observations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the formula in explicit algebraic form, carry out at least one worked example showing arithmetic steps and units, and present full tables (species, specific gravity, modulus, observations) so practitioners/engineers can apply results directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe instrument construction and operating principle clearly
rubrics_metrics.description: For the differential barometer: use a glass tube bent into an inverted siphon with parallel legs; cement extremities into bottoms of two equal cisterns (one closed with a small horizontal pipe, the other open); fill lower tube with water and upper legs with equal measures of oil to equalize the water surfaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the closed cistern's lateral pipe transmits external pressure (e.g., to a keyhole) and how pressure differences change water levels. State why oil+water amplifies variations (olive oil makes instrument ~11× more sensitive than water alone) and detail assembly dimensions (cistern diameter ~2 inches, internal tube diameter ≥ 1/4 inch).

rubrics_metrics.name: Calibrate instrument sensitivity via fluid densities and mixtures
rubrics_metrics.description: Sensitivity may be increased by altering the excess of the column of water above the oil: mix alcohol with water to reduce its specific gravity relative to oil (e.g., to 1/10, 1/15, etc.), or use different oils; at extreme attenuation the spirit may rest with no steadiness or even invert behaviour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the target specific-gravity relation for desired sensitivity (reference to 'proof' spirit), explain percentage amplification (oil vs water), and warn about limits of stability when spirit is too light. Provide examples of how choice of liquids affects scale of variations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt instruments for additional measurements with simple modifications
rubrics_metrics.description: By closing both cisterns and adding trumpet-mouthed lateral apertures, the differential barometer can serve as an anemometer; the original design was also intended to measure the force of heated air ascending in chimneys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the modification clearly (close cisterns, apply trumpet apertures) and the intended measured quantity (air current pressure/draft). Cite practical observations and phenomena (e.g., Flinders' observation of differing barometer readings with sea-breeze vs land-wind) to motivate applications.
